text: Every day, you want to get somewhere efficiently. Your brain instantly picks the shortest line on the map, because shorter always means faster, right? It just seems logical.
But then your navigation app suggests a route that looks… longer. It loops around, takes a side road, or goes a different way entirely. You instinctively question it.
Why would it do that? Your internal compass screams that the direct path is obviously superior. You might suspect the algorithm is broken, or just doesn't know better.
The truth is, the system isn't just looking at distance. It's constantly calculating *time costs*: traffic, lights, construction, and even future congestion.
It understands that a few extra miles on a clear road often beat fewer miles stuck in a jam. The cost is surrendering your intuitive "shortest path" logic.
So next time your map sends you on an unexpected detour, remember: it’s not about distance. It's about optimizing for time, making the invisible flow visible.
